records.name: THE LECH
records.note: Hold: CDB90 spans 15–16 April 1632, whereas Rain’s municipal account explicitly dates the battle to 14–15 April and places Tilly’s wound on the second day, followed by the imperial withdrawal that night. Keep the public 14–15 April extent; do not shift it to fit the source. The original initial-strength estimates, SW ARMY 33000 and IMP ARMY 27000, and personnel casualties 1000/3000 remain raw CDB90 observations. The city gives a different Swedish strength estimate; that numerical difference alone is not the reason for the hold.

records.name: ALTE VESTE
records.note: Hold: the source contains explicit active periods on 3 September 1632 (10:00–20:00) and 4 September (10:00–11:00). University of St Andrews SSNE 1969 directly establishes fighting on 3 September, and the Zirndorf municipal museum identifies Gustav Adolf’s army and Wallenstein’s imperial army. A separate metadata proposal corrects the public 9 September start to 3 September without inventing an end. This review has not independently established the source’s 4 September combat interval or the boundary between that action and withdrawal. CDB90 initial strengths SW ARMY 46000 / IMP ARMY 60000 and personnel casualties 4000 / 2000 are retained as source estimates, not published as a reviewed whole-battle comparison.

records.name: LUETZEN

records.name: NORDLINGEN I
records.note: Hold: CDB90 records only the 6 September 1634 fighting (05:30–12:30). The Geopark Ries brochure, published by Ostalbkreis, explicitly describes the Nördlingen museum’s 5–6 September battle; a contemporary 1634 pamphlet catalogued by the University of Warsaw also explicitly names both dates. The public already has 5–6 September and needs no correction. Do not shorten the whole battle to the final-day source phase. Original SW ARMY 25000 and SP & IMP ARMY 35000 initial personnel, with 12000 / 2000 personnel casualties, remain raw evidence; the imperial-Spanish aggregate must not later be duplicated across its constituent polities.

records.name: WITTSTOCK
records.note: Wittstock municipality explicitly equates 4 October Gregorian with 24 September Julian 1636 and identifies the combined Imperial-Saxon army versus Baner and Leslie's Swedish army. records.name: BREITENFELD II
records.note: Approve the exact whole battle after the separately proposed correction to 2 November 1642 Gregorian. The HAB/Freiburg scholarly diary introduction explicitly equates 23 October with 2 November and identifies Torstensson against Leopold Wilhelm and Piccolomini’s imperial-Saxon army. CDB90 IMP ARMY and SW ARMY are retained as two aggregate commands; no additional Saxon total is added. Both personnel strengths are initial-strength estimates, with no source reinforcements. The institutional evidence establishes chronology and force identity, not exact confirmation of the CDB90 30000/25000 strengths or 15000/5000 casualty estimates.

records.name: TUTTLINGEN
records.note: Chronology and casualty-scope hold. CDB and catalogue give 24 November 1643 only. ADB Mercy separates the attack on 24 November from Rantzau's surrender of 7,000 men on 25 November. CDB defender casualties are also 7,000, but their source attribution does not establish whether they exclude the next-day surrender. Do not promote a potentially multi-day complete loss into the one-day event. IMP ARMY would also require a local Bavarian-Imperial-Lorraine identity review.

A later Versailles painting title uses 3–9. The source row includes a last active period on 9 August and total losses, so the final combat date and total scope need resolution before promotion. No source date is silently changed.

records.name: SENEF
records.note: Hold pending an explicit end-of-day interpretation policy: CDB90 describes a 14-hour period from 11 August 1674 10:00 to exactly 12 August 00:00. The Seneffe museum’s educational account labels the battle the day of 11 August, ends the fighting around midnight, and distinguishes the following morning’s movements. This is potentially a timestamp-boundary representation of the same battle, not proof of a separate day of combat. Do not add 12 August to public metadata merely to satisfy the day-level gate. Original FR ARMY 50000 / DU ALLIED ARMY 70000 initial personnel and casualties 10000 / 14000 remain raw estimates. The museum’s mixed fictional narrative and factual boxes are not a primary eyewitness transcript; its differing casualty figures are not used to overwrite CDB90.

records.name: ENZHEIM
records.note: Reviewed full battle of 4 October 1674, Turenne against Bournonville, independently identified in the Entzheim municipal bulletin (December 2021, printed pp. 30–31). Both initial-strength rows cover this engagement: FR ARMY 22000 and IMP ALLIED ARMY 31700, with personnel casualties 3500 and 2500, not deaths. These remain CDB estimates: the municipal account gives roughly 6500 combined losses, so it is identity/date evidence and does not certify the CDB sum of 6000. Later Brandenburg reinforcements are not added. Each mixed field army remains a single local military unit; no component totals, equipment or tactical movements are inferred.

records.name: FEHRBELLIN
records.note: Approve the exact one-day Fehrbellin battle after replacing the published 19 July end with 28 June 1675. GHI dates the battle to 28 June; ZMSBw describes a short battle between the Swedish army and the Elector of Brandenburg’s predominantly cavalry force. The CDB90 6000 Brandenburg personnel are not an infantry count. Its Swedish 6400 estimate has a +72 percent qualifier (upper bound 11008), whereas ZMSBw gives 7000 infantry and 4000 cavalry. ZMSBw’s roughly 4000 Swedish losses explicitly include deserters; they do not replace CDB90’s 2500 personnel battle casualties. Differences of estimates and categories are retained, not treated as proof of exact agreement. Both CDB90 strengths are initial totals without source reinforcements.

records.name: THE BOYNE
records.note: Approve the exact whole battle on 11 July 1690 Gregorian, conditional on the separately proposed calendar correction. OPW explicitly labels 1 July Old Style; the Irish libraries’ visitor-centre account supplies 11 July in the modern calendar. Local force identities describe Williamite and Jacobite aggregate armies, not exclusively English troops or present-day states. OPW gives 36000 Williamite and 25000 Jacobite personnel; CDB90 retains its own 35000 and 23000 estimates and its distinct casualty estimates. The institutional total difference is disclosed rather than averaged or silently reconciled. Both source strengths are initial totals without reinforcements. The former five published participant entries are replaced by two aggregate coalition armies. Their original item/statement citations are retained with the corresponding aggregates, except Kingdom of Scotland (Q230791), whose ambiguous camp-level identity is preserved among battle metadata sources. No five-to-two identity retention is claimed and no unknown national component is added on top of either coalition total.

records.name: POLTAVA
records.note: Hold: the source uses 28 June 1709 without a declared calendar. The Presidential Library explicitly pairs 27 June with 8 July 1709; the cached Wikidata claims also identify 27 June as Julian and 8 July as Gregorian. A separate metadata proposal corrects the public date to 8 July. The Swedish Army Museum uses 28 June in its Poltava anniversary title, consistent with a distinct Swedish dating tradition, but this does not authorize an undocumented source-calendar conversion. CDB90 initial strengths SW ARMY 21500 / RUSS ARMY 80000 and personnel casualties 9600 / 1300 remain raw evidence. The library separates about 20000 Swedish battle participants from up to 10000 reserves and gives 42000 Russians; it also separates Russian killed and wounded. Therefore force coverage and the 1300 casualty category require further review independently of the date. No estimate is replaced, no reserve added, and no casualties converted into deaths.

records.name: DETTINGEN
records.note: Conservative force-scope hold, not proof that the CDB total is wrong. NAM identifies the Pragmatic Army as British, Hanoverian and Austrian and describes Austrian cavalry actually fighting at Dettingen. CDB labels its 35000 initial personnel only BR & HAN ARMY, under George II; neither the NAM account nor the tabulated CDB row establishes whether those 35000 include the Austrian contingent or describe the named British/Hanoverian subset. A shorter historical label may be incomplete, but renaming it Pragmatic Army would assert an unverified aggregate scope. Retain the raw estimate; do not add Austrian strength, divide the count, or approve proportional whole-camp representation until its inclusion is supported. The decision is about unresolved inclusion, not differences between published strength estimates.

records.name: SELMA
records.note: Conservative battle-versus-campaign scope hold supported by the U.S. Army Center of Military History. Bradley, The Civil War Ends, 1865, printed p. 50 gives 13480 cavalry departing on Wilson’s raid on 22 March and then records Croxton’s brigade moving separately to Tuscaloosa; p. 52 gives about 9000 in Long’s and Upton’s two divisions outside Selma on 2 April. CDB assigns 13500 initial personnel to US CAV CORPS MIL DIV MISSISSIPPI for the one-day battle, closely corresponding to the larger raid force rather than the two divisions present. The source also describes the defenders as cavalry, state troops and pressed local citizens, while CDB names CS CAV CORPS (ELMS); inclusion of the non-cavalry defenders in its 7000 is unresolved. This is a demonstrated detachment/force-scope issue, not merely different estimates. Keep the raw CDB counts, but do not use them as whole-battle proportional camps or substitute 9000/4000 automatically.
